# OpenSocrates 1.2.0

OpenSocrates 1.2.0 expands the same managed lifecycle beyond Claude and Codex
with packages for Google Antigravity, Cursor, Grok Build, and OpenCode.

## Google Antigravity and Cursor

- Antigravity gets an experimental, content-only global plugin validated with
  `agy 1.0.6`. It exposes one explicit `opensocrates` skill and 48 internal
  authored procedures.
- Cursor gets an experimental, content-only Agent Plugin with one
  `/opensocrates` skill and the same internal authored catalog.
- Neither package adds hooks, a native runtime, a background process, or a
  separate model call for automatic OpenSocrates selection. Antigravity's
  package shape was live-validated; Cursor's package contract is
  release-validated without a live invocation receipt.

## Grok Build

- Grok Build gets a dedicated native plugin with automatic same-turn skill
  selection and explicit `/opensocrates` invocation.
- Automatic and explicit headless activation were live-validated on Grok Build
  1.0.3. TUI host-hook execution was observed, while TUI native-skill and
  subagent-propagation receipts remain pending.
- The shipped Grok package is content-only and owns only
  `~/.grok/plugins/opensocrates`; it does not edit unrelated Grok
  configuration, hooks, plugins, or marketplaces.

## OpenCode

- OpenCode 1.18.18+ automatically discovers the generated global plugin and
  native `opensocrates` Agent Skill.
- The stable `chat.message` bridge can inject one complete authored procedure
  into the same model turn after bounded local judgment classification.
- Mechanical, malformed, oversized, timed-out, and exceptional inputs fail
  open. The bridge makes no extra model, network, subprocess, or recursive
  OpenCode call.
- A real `opencode run` validated the exact generated bridge on OpenCode
  1.18.18 with DeepSeek V4 Flash in both `opencode run` and the interactive
  TUI. Native skill invocation remains unverified (discovery was validated).

## Lifecycle and release safety

- `install`, `status`, `verify`, `update`, `remove`, rollback, automatic
  updates, and `--host all` now cover Antigravity, Claude, Codex, Cursor, Grok
  Build, and OpenCode.
- Every host has an exact ownership boundary. The installer preserves unrelated
  host files and configuration; in particular, it never rewrites
  `opencode.json`.
- Host-qualified candidate assets define an exact `--host all` transaction, so
  pre-release validation never mixes candidate packages with public-release
  downloads for other locally available hosts.
- Package and installed inventories, checksums, manifests, generated content,
  ownership, deterministic archives, and release workflow assets are checked.

```sh
npx --yes opensocrates@1.2.0 install --host opencode
npx --yes opensocrates@1.2.0 install --host grok
npx --yes opensocrates@1.2.0 install --host cursor
npx --yes opensocrates@1.2.0 install --host antigravity
npx --yes opensocrates@1.2.0 update --host all
```

See the dedicated
[Antigravity](../../docs/antigravity-support.md),
[Cursor](../../docs/cursor-support.md),
[Grok Build](../../docs/grok-support.md), and
[OpenCode](../../docs/opencode-support.md) support boundaries for exact
validation levels and remaining limitations.
